entries.name: Luvaghn Brown

expected_cases.charges: Sit-in at a Jackson Walgreens lunch counter — arrested at sixteen, July 11, 1961; a later 1961 arrest picketing outside the Jackson fairgrounds also noted.
expected_cases.convicted: Unresolved — the arrest is documented; the disposition is not established in the CRDL record
expected_cases.sentence: Arrested 1961-07-11. The Civil Rights Digital Library establishes the arrest and the identification photograph but not the disposition, any transfer to Parchman, or the release date — unresolved pending court, jail, or penitentiary records.

new_case.charges: Contempt of court for refusing to leave a bench reserved for white spectators during the Diane Nash Bevel proceedings in Jackson.
new_case.sentence: Sentenced to 30 days at hard labor and a $100 fine. The Mississippi Free Press reported his May 21 arrest and release from the Hinds County prison farm on the evening of July 3, 1962. This is a separate detention from the July 1961 sit-in arrest.

entries.rationale: Mississippi Free Press July 14, 1962, page 4, explicitly names Luvaghn Brown, dates arrest May 21 and release evening July 3. Add a separate case, preserving the original 1961 arrest. The imposed 30-day sentence is not substituted for the observed 43-day elapsed custody.
